AssetKind.description:
Within an asset-generation case, the shape of the asset the model draws.

A case is one of: a single 2D sprite, a 2D sprite sheet, a single static 3D
voxel model, or a rigged/animatable 3D voxel model — never a mix, and not a
per-variant choice: it is a property of the whole version, chosen by the
`asset_kind` field. A [`Self::SpriteSheet`] case additionally declares a
`[sheet]` table (the frame grid and the named animation sequences); the two
voxel kinds declare a `[voxel]` table (the bounding volume), and
[`Self::VoxelAnimation`] additionally declares a `[model]` table (the parts,
joints, and clips of the rig). Defaults to [`Self::Sprite`] so a manifest that
predates the discriminator — and every non-asset-generation case — resolves
unchanged.

oneOf.description: One sprite drawn onto the whole canvas (the original asset-generation shape).

A grid of animation frames drawn onto the canvas, sliced into the named
sequences the `[sheet]` table declares.

A single static 3D voxel model, drawn one voxel operation at a time with the
`voxel` binary. Declares a `[voxel]` table (the bounding volume). Rendered as
an auto-rotating 3D model.

A rigged, animatable 3D voxel model: named parts in a parent/child hierarchy
with named joints a consuming game drives at runtime (for example a tank's
`turret_yaw`), drawn with the `voxel-anim` binary. Declares a `[voxel]` table
and a `[model]` table (the required parts and joints the model must produce,
on top of which it may add its own).

A static surface-meshed 3D model built with the **marching cubes** `mc`
binary: the model composites a signed-distance field of CSG primitives, which
the mesher extracts to a per-model `.glb`. Declares a `[voxel]` table
(the field bounds) and no `[model]`. Marching cubes yields a chunky, faceted
**low-poly** surface.

A rigged, animatable surface-meshed 3D model built with the **marching cubes**
`mc-anim` binary. Like [`Self::VoxelAnimation`] but each part is a meshed
field extracted to its own `.glb`; declares a `[voxel]` and a `[model]`
table.

A static surface-meshed 3D model built with the **surface nets** `sn` binary.
Declares a `[voxel]` table and no `[model]`. Surface nets yields a smooth,
watertight mid-fidelity surface with uniform triangle density.

A rigged, animatable surface-meshed 3D model built with the **surface nets**
`sn-anim` binary. Like [`Self::VoxelAnimation`] but each part is a meshed
field; declares a `[voxel]` and a `[model]` table.

A static surface-meshed 3D model built with the **dual contouring** `dc`
binary. Declares a `[voxel]` table and no `[model]`. Dual contouring yields a
high-fidelity surface that preserves sharp edges and corners.

A rigged, animatable surface-meshed 3D model built with the **dual contouring**
`dc-anim` binary. Like [`Self::VoxelAnimation`] but each part is a meshed
field; declares a `[voxel]` and a `[model]` table.

A high-resolution 2D interface asset (or kit of elements) painted with the
`paint`/`ui` binaries. Declares a `[canvas]` (base element size) and an
optional `[ui]` table (the kit's elements). Judged on the emitted flattened
PNG(s) plus `ui.json`.

A tileable PBR material — a set of maps (base color, normal, roughness, …) —
painted with the `texture`/`pbr` binaries. Declares a `[material]` table (no
`[canvas]`/`[voxel]`). Judged on the emitted maps plus `material.json`.

A skinned character (marching cubes): one whole-body field bound to a
model-invented skeleton, deformed by linear-blend skinning. Declares a
`[voxel]` and a `[model]` table but emits a **single** `mesh.glb` + `rig.json`
(not per-part).
A skinned character (surface nets). See [`Self::McSkinned`].
A skinned character (dual contouring). See [`Self::McSkinned`].

A 2D particle effect authored with the `particle-2d` binary. Declares a
`[particle]` table (a planar field). Judged on the emitted `system.json`.

A 3D particle effect authored with the `particle-3d` binary. Declares a
`[particle]` table (a volume). Judged on the emitted `system.json`.

A procedurally-synthesized sound effect authored with the `sfx-synth` binary.
Declares an `[audio]` table. Judged on the emitted `clip.wav`.

A sample-library sound effect authored with the `sfx-sample` binary. Declares
an `[audio]` table (naming its `sample_pack`). Judged on the emitted `clip.wav`.

A short piece of music authored with the `music` sequencer binary. Declares an
`[audio]` table (naming its `instrument_bank`). Judged on the emitted
`clip.wav` (and portable `clip.mid`).

A rigged, animated **skinned character** authored by driving **headless Blender**
through its Python API — the first Blender-based asset kind. The model writes a
`build.py` (a `bpy` script) that builds the character mesh, an armature, skin
weights, and one Action per required animation, then runs the `tcab-blend` runner
to export a single **`character.glb`** (a standard skinned + animated glTF 2.0)
plus a `model.png` preview. Unlike the CSG skinned kinds (`mc-skinned` …), there
is **no operation log**: `build.py` is the recorded authoring trace, re-run for
provenance. Declares a `[voxel]` table (reused as the character's bounding box)
and a `[model]` table (the required animations); judged on the emitted glTF, never
an op-log replay.

A static **hard-surface prop** authored by driving headless Blender through a
`build.py` script — a weapon, crate, pickup, or emplacement. Like every Blender
kind it writes a `build.py` and runs `tcab-blend`, but it emits a **static**,
unrigged native glTF (`model.glb`): no armature, no skin, and **no animations**,
so it declares **no `[model]` table**. Reuses the `[voxel]` table as a bounding
box. Judged on the emitted glTF (a well-formed static mesh); `build.py` is the
recorded trace, re-run for provenance.

A **rigidly-articulated mechanism** authored by driving headless Blender through a
`build.py` script — a turret, blast door, crane, or mech. It emits a native glTF
(`model.glb`) whose motion is baked as standard **glTF node-hierarchy animations**
(each part posed about its pivot by parenting, **not** skin deformation and **not**
a Test-Cabinet `rig.json`), so a game plays the clips natively. Declares a
`[voxel]` bounding box and a `[model]` table of required animations, reconciled
against the emitted glTF; `build.py` is re-run for provenance.

AudioSpec.description:
The resolved `[audio]` of an audio asset-generation case: the rendered clip's
output format and (for the sample/instrument kinds) the baked palette.

instrumentBank.description: For `music`: the baked instrument bank (`name@version`). `None` otherwise.

maxDurationMs.description: Cap on the rendered clip's length in milliseconds.

samplePack.description: For `sfx-sample`: the baked sample pack (`name@version`). `None` otherwise.

CaseOut.description:
One held-out scored case of a performance case: the store-relative keys of the
`input` scenario fed to the engine and the `expected` oracle state its output
is checked against. Mirrors core's wire `CaseBody`, so a resolved version
round-trips its scored set through to the runner's [`materialize_version`].

fuelCeiling.description:
The case's resolved run ceiling (`fuel_limit * fuel_runway`), carried so the
driver grades against the same ceiling the manifest declared.

kind.description:
Which phase the case belongs to — a correctness pre-flight `smoke` test or a
scored `stress` case — carried so the driver runs the smoke gate before the
stress cases. Defaults to `stress` for versions ingested before smoke tests.

CheckAction.description:
A single action that drives a served implementation toward a view.

Serializes to the JSON shape the browser driver consumes (an internally
tagged `{ "type": … }` object); see `packages/browser-driver/driver.mjs`.

oneOf.description: Pause for `ms` milliseconds.
Press and release a key (Playwright key name, e.g. `Enter`, `ArrowUp`).
Hold a key down for `ms` milliseconds, then release it.

ms.description: How long to hold it, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: Click a logical-pixel point on the page.

ErratumOut.description:
A known-issue erratum in the §1.2 wire shape (see
[`test_cabinet_core::test_case::Erratum`]).

excludeFromScore.description: Whether the linked review point is excluded from scoring for the version.

review.description: The review verdict id the erratum concerns, or absent when untied to a point.

variant.description: The variant slug the erratum is scoped to, or absent for all variants.

ErratumSeverity.description: How serious a known-issue [`Erratum`] is, surfaced as a badge on the site.

oneOf.description: A note or minor caveat that does not meaningfully affect a run.
A real but limited issue — the default.
A significant issue that materially affects the case or its scoring.

InstrumentationOut.description: The `[instrumentation]` handle in the §1.2 wire shape.

handle.description: The `window` property name the debug API is installed on (no `window.` prefix).

tickHz.description:
The case's fixed simulation rate in whole ticks per second, when it declares
one — what lets the validation runtime relate exact stepping to real time.
Omitted for a real-time-clocked case.

MaterialSpec.description:
The resolved `[material]` of a `material` asset-generation case: the tileable PBR
material's output resolution, seamlessness, and emitted channels.

background.description: Preview clear color: `transparent` or a hex color.

maps.description:
The channels the material emits, in declared order. Always includes
`base-color`.

size.description: Square map resolution in pixels (a power of two).

tile.description: Whether the maps are authored seamlessly (wrap toroidally).

PackageOut.description:
A runtime package a case ships into its runs, exposed for the console's Inputs
tab: its npm name and the UI-only description of what it provides (never seeded
into a run).

ParticleSpec.description:
The resolved `[particle]` of a particle asset-generation case: the field the
effect plays in and its playback timing. [`Self::depth`] is `Some` for
`particle-3d` (a volume) and `None` for `particle-2d` (a planar field).

background.description: Preview clear color: `transparent` or a hex color.

depth.description: Field extent along z. `Some` for `particle-3d`, `None` for `particle-2d`.

looping.description: Whether the effect loops (steady-state) or is one-shot.

ReferenceKind.description: How a reference view's source is turned into the seeded/served artifact.

oneOf.description:
An HTML mockup rendered to a PNG screenshot. The served media is always an
image.
A static image file used as-is.
A static video file (`mp4`) used as-is.

kind.description: How the reference is produced (`rendered`, `image`, or `video`).

mediaUrl.description: The URL path the reference media is served under.

subItems.description:
Name-only sub-items the reviewer grades this item by, each an
independently scored pass/fail point. Empty for an item graded as a whole.

validation.description:
The item's automated-validation driver, when it opts into auto-validation:
the reporter-side debug script (by its version-folder-relative key) and its
declared media outputs. Served so the driver's validator can fetch, materialize,
and run it against the build's debug API. Absent for a human-judged item.

ReviewOutputOut.description: One media output of a [`ReviewValidationOut`] script in the §1.2 wire shape.

ReviewValidationOut.description:
A review item's automated-validation driver in the §1.2 wire shape: the
version-folder-relative debug `script` key the driver fetches (like an asset) and
its declared media `outputs`.

SpecKind.description:
What role a seeded spec file plays, so a reader can tell an instruction the
model reads from an executable starter it edits and runs.

This is a **presentation** distinction only — every kind is seeded identically
(copied to its `dest`) and the harness treats them the same. It exists so the
Inputs surfaces can tag a starter script (for example the Blender case's
`build.py`, whose `dest` deliberately coincides with `[output].actions`)
distinctly from a prose spec.

oneOf.description:
A specification the model reads — prose (a brief) or any other guidance.
The default when a `[[spec]]` entry declares no `kind`.

An executable starter file the model edits in place and runs, seeded as the
case's own trace (for example a `bpy` `build.py`). Surfaced as "Script".

kind.description:
The seeded file's role (`spec`/`script`), so the console's Inputs tab can
tag it. Presentation only.

StoredContract.description:
The submission contract of an adversarial or performance case persisted in a
[`StoredManifest`]. Path fields are forward-slashed run-workspace-relative keys.
Adversarial carries the per-tick `world`/`action` schemas; performance carries
the per-scenario `input`/`output` schemas. The pairs are `Option` so the two
types coexist on one stored shape (only one pair is set).

action.description: Adversarial only: the seeded `action` schema path.

entry.description:
The exported function invoked once per tick (adversarial) or once per
scenario (performance).

input.description: Performance only: the seeded `input` (scenario) schema path.

output.description: Performance only: the seeded `output` (state) schema path.

world.description: Adversarial only: the seeded `world` observation schema path.

StoredMatch.description:
How an adversarial case pairs implementations into matches, persisted in a
[`StoredManifest`].

structure.description: How the field is paired (for example `round-robin`).

StoredReplay.description:
How an adversarial case renders a recorded match for browser playback,
persisted in a [`StoredManifest`].

renderer.description: The run-workspace-relative path the renderer is seeded to, forward-slashed.

StoredSandbox.description:
The sandbox limits of an adversarial or performance case persisted in a
[`StoredManifest`]. Adversarial meters per tick (`fuel_per_tick`); performance
meters per scenario (`fuel_limit`). Both fuel fields are `Option` so the two
types coexist (only one is set).

fuelLimit.description: Performance only: the wasmtime fuel ceiling for a whole scenario.

fuelPerTick.description: Adversarial only: the wasmtime fuel ceiling for a single tick.

StoredSimulation.description:
The simulation-loop configuration of an adversarial case persisted in a
[`StoredManifest`].

timestepMs.description: The fixed, faked delta handed to the game logic each tick (milliseconds).

description.description:
Optional prose for this point (categories grammar); absent for a legacy
name-only sub-item.

proof.description: Optional submitted proof paired with this point.

reference.description: Optional expected reference paired with this point.

validation.description:
The sub-item's automated-validation driver, when it opts into auto-validation.
Same shape as [`ReviewItemOut::validation`] but keyed to this sub-item's verdict.
Absent for a human-judged sub-item.

weight.description:
How many points this point is worth. A category's weight is the sum of its
items' weights.

UiElementSpec.description:
A resolved `[[ui.element]]`: one named element of a UI kit, its size, and an
optional fixed nine-slice.

nineSlice.description:
The fixed stretchable insets, when the case declares them (otherwise the
model authors them with `ui set-nine-slice`).

UiSpec.description:
The resolved `[ui]` of a `ui` asset-generation case: the kit of named elements
the model paints. Empty [`Self::elements`] means the case is a single implicit
element (the whole `[canvas]`).

elements.description: The declared elements, in declared order. Empty for a single-image case.

domains.description:
The variant's own scoring domains, on top of the case's common
[`VersionResponse::domains`]. Rated only when this variant is selected.

prompt.description: The variant's prompt, rendered as a real run receives it.

referenceBuild.description:
The absolute URL of this variant's authored **reference implementation** — the
correct, deployed static build (the case-variant analogue of a run's
`playableBuild`), served on the console's "Reference" tab. `None` when the
variant declares no `reference_implementation`, or has one but it has not been
deployed yet. Written out-of-band by `tcab publish-reference` and read from the
`case_reference_build` table — never resolved from the manifest and never
seeded into a run.

voxel.description:
The variant's bounding-volume override, when it declares its own `[voxel]`
(the size axis behind a case's half/base/double variants). `None` inherits
the case's common [`VersionResponse::voxel`].

VoxelSpec.description:
The resolved `[voxel]` of a voxel asset-generation case: the bounding volume
the model draws into, the 3D analog of [`CanvasSpec`]. `background` is the
clear color behind the rendered preview PNG (the voxel volume itself always
starts empty); it is kept as the manifest string — validated to parse — so the
resolved version stays serializable without depending on the voxel library's
color type.

background.description: Preview clear color: `transparent` or a hex color.

depth.description: Volume extent along z, in voxels.

height.description: Volume extent along y (up), in voxels.

width.description: Volume extent along x, in voxels.

description:
The resolved, fully-rendered definition of one test-case version: the body of
`GET /test-cases/{slug}/{version}`. Everything a reporter needs to present the
case — its metadata, the per-test-type contract/sandbox shapes, the rendered
prompt and seeded specs, and every variant, reference, proof, check, and
reviewer item — resolved as a real run receives them.

cases.description:
A performance case's held-out scored set — each case's `input` scenario and
`expected` oracle state, by store-relative key. Empty (and omitted) for
every other type. The runner fetches these like assets and the performance
validator scores the engine against them; they are never seeded into a run.

changelog.description:
The version's own changelog entry (its `changelog.md` body), inlined.
Always present — a changelog is required on every version. The console
aggregates every version's entry into the case's changelog tab.

errata.description:
Known-issue errata recorded for this version after it shipped. Site-facing:
shown on the case's Errata tab and, where relevant, to reviewers scoring a
run of the version. Empty when the version has none.

instrumentation.description:
The case's `[instrumentation]` debug-API handle, when it mandates one for
automated validation. Reporter-side (never seeded into a run): served so the
driver's validator knows which `window` handle to drive. Absent for a case with
no auto-validated items.

packages.description:
The Test Cabinet runtime packages this case ships into every run, each with
a UI-only description. Shown on the console's Inputs tab; empty for a case
that declares none.

title: VersionResponse
